steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Grease two 9-inch round cake pans and line with waxed paper.
Mix flour and baking powder in a bowl.
Beat white sugar, butter, and gelatin together in a separate bowl until fluffy; add eggs, one at a time, beating well with each addition.
Stir alternately flour mixture then milk, into sugar mixture to form a smooth batter. Stir vanilla extract and strawberries into batter until combined.
Divide batter between prepared cake pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of both cakes comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes; cool completely.
Stir cream cheese, white chocolate, and heavy whipping cream in a saucepan over medium heat until combined and white chocolate is melted, about 5 minutes.
Stir confectioners' sugar into cream cheese mixture until a smooth frosting forms. Allow to cool and set.
Spread a layer of frosting over the top of one cake. Place the second cake on top of frosting layer. Frost the top of second cake and sides of both cakes with remaining frosting.

raw_recipe.headline: White Chocolate Strawberry Cake
raw_recipe.description: The moist, flavorful strawberry cake and rich white chocolate frosting combine to create a decadent dessert.

review.reviewBody: I baked this cake for a colleague at work because it was her birthday and everyone, I mean everyone, loved it! It is dense and with the frosting it is a very rich cake. I ended up having to make more frosting because I didn't have quite enough. That might have been because I baked a 9" round and not 8". My husband made a special trip to my workplace at lunch just so he could get a piece. He said he knew it would be good because he saw what went into it. I did not have any problem with the purée sinking to the bottom of the cake. It is a keeper!

I made this into cupcakes. The cake recipe was great, very tasty and a big hit! So the icing recipe didn't make much sense to me, and other reviewers wrote how hard it was to manage, so I melted some white chocolate chips and folded it into a regular cream cheese icing recipe. Turned out great, and I'd definitely make it again!

I made this as a test run before I make it for a birthday party. The crumb/texture turned out great. My only complaint is that it was really sweet, BUT that may have had more to do with the fact that I sweetened my strawberries before I froze them. My next attempt will use less sugar.
Update: used about 1/2 C less sugar and sweetened, 
frozen, strawberries and everything still turned out extremely sweet. If I make this again I may gamble with a whole cup less sugar.
I used white chocolate chips for the frosting because that's what I had. Turned out fine. The cake was really good. Will make again

The cake is very good. The frosting didn’t turn out so well for me. Although it does taste very good, it’s not very smooth and looks horrible when I put it on the cake. I don’t think 3 tablespoons is enough heavy cream for 4 cups of confectionery sugar. I had to keep adding more. It seemed smooth when it was done but was not smooth after it cooled and tried to spread it.
I felt the cake was not as moist as other Strawberry Cakes I have made in the past. The Frosting was delicious however hard to work with when the white chocolate started to harden.
I made this cake last year and my family loved it. The only I did differently was I made my own butter cream frosting. My family doesn’t eat chocolate. Wonderful recipe!
I made this for my husband’s birthday. I followed the recipe precisely but added one additional stick of unsalted butter and used four extra large eggs.

Haven't tasted the cake yet but the frosting was very stiff and not spreadable. Even after adding 2 tsp milk it was difficult to work with. I did sub 3/4 cup of white chocolate chips when the store did not have squares but I don't see how this would be an issue. The flavor however was superb.
The cake was perfect. The frosting was dry and hard to spread.

I followed the recipe for the cake exactly and it was very very thick and dense, it tasted too much like flour, and the icing instructions weren't very clear. By that I mean it said to add the confectioner's sugar into the cream cheese and chocolate mix but didn't tell you to take it off the heat so I added everything thinking I was supposed to let it all melt together...I took it off to let it cool like instructed and within 10 minutes it was literally rock hard, very hard and I knew there was no way I'd be able to frost with it. So unfortunately all that icing had to be thrown away and I had to make another trip to the store to get more sugar. All that said it is still pretty tasty but I can't eat very much of it at one time...I got a moderate slice and could only eat about half as it's so thick. I probably won't be making this again.

Absolutely Amazing! So moist and flavorful and super easy to prepare. Made this for my younger brothers going away party everyone loved it. The frosting was simple to make and tasted great not too sweet and not too plain. Definitely keeping this recipe and will make again.
